div.head: Af 1
div.ab: II. Æt ærestan we lærað, þæt mæst ðearf ís, þæt æghwelc mon his að ⁊ his wed wærlice healde.
II. Æt ærestan we lærað, ðæt mæst þearf is, þæt æghwilc man his að ⁊ his wedd wærlice healde.
Inprimis est, quod maxime necessarium est: cuicumque fidelium fidem et iuramentum suum multa conuenit obseruantia custodire.
Æt ærestan we lærað, þæt mæst ðearf ís, þæt æghwelc mon his að ⁊ his wed wærlice healde.
{II} Æt ærestan we lærað, þæt mæst ðearf ís, þæt æghwelce mon his að ⁊ his wed wærlice healde.
Zuerst lehren wir, was zumeist nöthig ist, dass jedermann seinen Eid und sein rechtsförmliches Versprechen sorgfältig halte.
First we teach what is most needful: that everyone keep his oath and his formal pledge carefully.
In the first place we enjoin you, as a matter of supreme importance, that every man shall abide carefully by his oath and his pledge.
First we direct, what is most necessary, that each man keep carefully his oath and pledge.
First we instruct, that it is most needful, that each man should prudently keep his oath and his vow.

note.label: see also
note.quote: Compare Ine §40. See also §1 and n. 14.

note.label: linked with
note.quote: Exeter's laws on surety and theft were intimately linked with Alfred's 'oath and pledge'

note.label: cf.
note.quote: Provisional loss of goods to friends is envisaged by Edward the Elder for those accused of theft who have no surety.

note.label: refers to
note.quote: yet II Ew 5 pretty clearly refers to Af 1, whose ramifications can be shown to extend to theft

note.label: alludes to (but modifies)
note.quote: Edward’s clause is one of several that allude to the domboc. But it may not ... be assumed that Edward’s understanding of að and wedd is the same as that underlying Alfred §1.

note.label: like
note.quote: convicted thieves get forty days in prison, like breakers of Alfred’s að 7 wed (1, 5)

note.label: may be quoting
note.quote: ‘To carefully keep one’s oath and pledge’, in words Wulfstan may be quoting from Alfred’s law (1, 16, 18)

note.seg: Laut des Wortes ‘Zuerst’ will Bisheriges als Einleitung gelten. Also ist die Zahl II unauthentisch; s. o. S. 40 Sp. 1; Af El 49, 6¹
The word ‘First’ shows that what precedes is meant to count as an introduction. The number II is therefore not authentic; see above p. 40 col. 1; Af El 49, 6¹
‘dass’ Thorpe, Schmid gegen Q und Frühere
‘that’ Thorpe, Schmid, against Q and earlier editors
fideles in Q sind entweder ‘Gläubige’, was zum kirchlichen Inhalt des Satzes und dem klerikalen Geiste des Bisherigen passt, oder nach Agnormann. Latein: ‘Untertanen’.
fideles in Q are either ‘the faithful’, which suits the ecclesiastical content of the sentence and the clerical spirit of what precedes, or, following Anglo-Norman Latin, ‘subjects’.
nicht ‘wahrhaft’, vielmehr ‘um-(vor)-sichtig, bedacht’ vielleicht ‘mit Unterscheidung’ des Falles 1, 1 von 1, 2
not ‘truly’, but rather ‘circumspectly (cautiously), with deliberation’, perhaps ‘with discrimination’ between the case of 1, 1 and that of 1, 2
